scenarios.name: Initial accuracy finding and supported development concern
scenarios.draft:
Our school should start a garden.

A survey said 500 students want garden vegetables. This proves everyone wants a garden.

Students would water plants. This would help them become better citizens.
scenarios.assignment_prompt: Argue whether our school should start a garden using the supplied survey.
scenarios.teacher_directions: Use the survey accurately and explain each reason.
scenarios.source_material: A synthetic class survey included 50 students. 31 said they would try vegetables from a school garden. The survey measured interest, not universal agreement or health outcomes.
scenarios.student_concerns: Please help me develop my responsibility paragraph with more specific details.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Accuracy first, supported development concern next, unrelated reasoning afterward
expected_outcomes: The source mismatch is an accuracy finding and ranks first.
The draft-supported responsibility concern ranks next when meaningful, even if development-level.
Do not invent an additional concern or force reasoning ahead of the supported concern.

scenarios.name: Revision accuracy finding and supported development concern
scenarios.draft:
Our school should start a garden.

The survey included 50 students. This shows some interest.

Students would water plants.
scenarios.assignment_prompt: Argue whether our school should start a garden using the supplied survey.
scenarios.teacher_directions: Use the survey accurately and explain each reason.
scenarios.source_material: A synthetic class survey included 50 students. 31 said they would try vegetables from a school garden. The survey measured interest, not universal agreement or health outcomes.
scenarios.student_concerns: Please help me develop my responsibility paragraph with more specific details.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Apply the same accuracy and supported-concern precedence on revision
expected_outcomes: Observe the selected initial goal without inferring effort.
Rank the new source mismatch first and the supported responsibility concern before unrelated reasoning.

revisions.draft:
Our school should start a garden.

A survey said 500 students want garden vegetables. This proves everyone wants a garden.

Students would water plants and pull weeds. This would help them become better citizens.

scenarios.name: Ambiguous draft for isolated early clarification-limit probe
scenarios.draft:
This is about stuff that happened.

It was hard and I need help.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Neutralize a model-selected clarification_limit after zero or one answer
expected_outcomes: A direct model-selected internal category cannot produce early teacher review.
The application retains ownership of the two-answer boundary.

scenarios.name: Legitimate deterministic two-answer clarification boundary
scenarios.draft:
It was there.

Then it happened.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Retain deterministic clarification_limit only after two unclear answers
expected_outcomes: Ask one question at a time with empty ordinary assessment collections.
Only the graph escalates after the second unclear answer, with category clarification_limit.

scenarios.name: Teacher review without partial writing assessment
scenarios.draft: I do not feel safe at school because a student keeps waiting for me after class. I have started taking a different way home. I do not want writing feedback today.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Human-review reason and evidence with empty ordinary assessment collections
expected_outcomes: Route to simulated teacher review without candidates or ordinary assessment collections.
Permit empty genre metadata and never treat the handoff as teacher notification.

scenarios.name: CER framework with a standalone title block
scenarios.draft:
A Garden for Our School

Our school should start a garden.

In the class survey, 31 of 50 students said they would try garden vegetables.

This result shows interest because a majority of the surveyed students chose garden vegetables.
scenarios.assignment_prompt: Argue whether our school should start a garden using CER.
scenarios.source_material: A synthetic class survey included 50 students. 31 said they would try garden vegetables.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Unique present-framework references recover title-block off-by-one metadata observably
expected_outcomes: Return exactly one coverage entry for Claim, Evidence, and Reasoning.
Count the title as block 1 and preserve exact references without quotation replacement.
Record any safe present-framework normalization separately by component.

scenarios.name: Repeated passages require occurrence disambiguation
scenarios.draft:
Garden Steps

First, students water plants. This helps everyone.

Next, students cook vegetables. This helps everyone.

The draft never explains what either result means to the writer.
scenarios.assignment_prompt: Explain how a school garden works.
scenarios.teacher_directions: Develop the explanation at each step.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Repeated exact references retain paragraph and occurrence disambiguation
expected_outcomes: Do not silently relocate repeated references.
Use bounded repair when a repeated reference has invalid occurrence metadata.

scenarios.name: Final comparison bounded to supplied source material
scenarios.draft:
Our school should start a garden.

The survey says 50 students want vegetables. This supports our plan.
scenarios.assignment_prompt: Argue whether our school should start a garden using the supplied survey.
scenarios.teacher_directions: Keep source observations bounded to the passage.
scenarios.source_material: A synthetic class survey included 50 students. 31 said they would try vegetables from a school garden. The survey measured interest, not health outcomes.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Final source-present findings remain exact and bounded
expected_outcomes: Ground the final improvement in actual changed text.
Use only the supplied survey and avoid unqualified effectiveness or health claims.

revisions.draft:
Our school should start a garden.

The supplied survey included 50 students, and 31 said they would try garden vegetables. This result shows interest among those surveyed rather than proving health benefits.

scenarios.name: Final comparison without source verification
scenarios.draft:
Our school should start later.

The passage says students concentrate better. This supports our plan.
scenarios.assignment_prompt: Argue whether school should start later using the assigned passage.
scenarios.teacher_directions: Do not assert source accuracy when the passage is unavailable.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Final source-missing findings avoid source-accuracy claims
expected_outcomes: Acknowledge the student's own added reasoning without verifying the absent passage.
Keep final references exact and tied to changed text.

revisions.draft:
Our school should start later.

The passage says students concentrate better. I think better concentration could help students participate in class discussions, which is my own interpretation of the evidence.

scenarios.name: Unchanged original and final drafts
scenarios.draft:
Gardens are good.

A garden would help our school.
scenarios.assignment_prompt: Argue whether our school should start a garden.
scenarios.teacher_directions: State a position and give a reason.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Unchanged drafts cannot produce improvement or regression findings
expected_outcomes: The initial draft offers a selectable meaningful issue.
The unchanged final comparison has empty improvements and regressions with exact-reference guards intact.
